name: Projected Double Density or Projected Average Degree
definition: The **projected double density** of a concept class is defined as the maximum over all projections of the averaged degree of the $1$-inclusion graph.
origin_references: The underlying one-inclusion-graph density is central in the work of Haussler, Littlestone, and Warmuth (1988, 1994); taking the maximum over coordinate projections is the catalogue's p-monotonic envelope construction.

p_monotonic.proof: Every coordinate projection of pi_T(H) is a coordinate projection pi_U(H) of the original class, for some U contained in T. Thus the collection over which the maximum defining the projected double density of pi_T(H) is taken is contained in the collection for H.

monotonic.proof: Counterexample: let G={0000,0001,0010,0100,0110,1000,1001} and H=G union {1111}. Exhausting the coordinate projections gives dens^p(G)=16/7 (attained on the full domain) but dens^p(H)=2. Hence adjoining a concept can decrease the parameter.

c_monotonic.proof: Counterexample: for H={00000,00010,00011,00100,00110,01000,01010,01100,01101,01110,01111,10000,10001,10010,10100,11000,11111}, exhaustive projection gives dens^p(H)=40/13. Conditioning the last coordinate to 0 and deleting it gives a class with projected double density 19/6>40/13.

doubly_monotonic.proof: Doubly monotonicity requires subfamily monotonicity, which is refuted by the recorded counterexample.

strictly_monotonic.proof: Strict monotonicity requires doubly monotonicity, which fails.
